campaign_name: I've Managed Fine — Six Objections, Six Films

cadence.set_by: Six drops across eight days (2026-09-06 to 2026-09-13), roughly every 36 hours with the times walked around the clock so the same objection is not always shown to the same daypart. Weekend mornings and weekday evenings are deliberate: this audience is behind a counter during business hours.

publish_arming.note: Queue script creates DRAFTS unarmed. Conversion to a live schedule requires FAMTASTIC_MARKETING_PUBLISH=true on the operator host. Provider IDs in this source file are recorded draft evidence, not a fresh live-provider read-back; every drop remains approval.publish=false and any reconciliation block must be resolved before a later owner review.

media_resolution.note: Films are gitignored (.gitignore: *.mp4) and exist only on the operator workstation under marketing/campaigns/ive-managed-fine/videos/. They are reproducible from source with marketing/hyperframes/ive-managed-fine/scripts/stage-assets.sh, build-narration.py, `hyperframes render`, and scripts/voice/narrate-film.sh. A drop whose primary media is missing is reported BLOCKED by name; it is never posted image-only by fallback.

drops.label: Drop 1 — Sat 9:30 AM ET: "I've managed fine for thirty years."
drops.theme: Objection 1 — thirty years is true, and it is the point
drops.headline: You have managed fine for thirty years. The way people look for you changed three times.

copy.facebook_instagram:
"I've managed fine for thirty years."

You have. That is not in question, and nobody at FAMtastic thinks otherwise.

Here is the part worth thinking about. The customers who found you over those thirty years did not find you the same way twice. Some found you in a phone book. Some heard your name from a neighbor. The ones arriving now are looking on a phone — and that is the only one of the three you are not on.

Same business. Three different front doors.

What a small business website is actually for, in plain terms:
https://famtasticdesigns.com/blog/what-should-a-small-business-website-do/

Web Basics is a one-time $199 — about 55 cents a day across the first year. One page, one year of managed hosting, and a domain that is yours. First year $199, then $9.99 a month, plus the domain. Business email and maintenance are separate.

drops.label: Drop 2 — Sun 4:00 PM ET: "My customers know where I am."
drops.theme: Objection 2 — the ones you have, yes; the ones who moved in last year, no
drops.headline: Your customers know where you are. The family that moved in last year does not.

copy.facebook_instagram:
"My customers know where I am."

The ones you already have, yes. They have known for years and they are not the question.

The question is the family that moved onto that street last year. They looked on a phone at nine at night, when your sign was dark and your door was locked. Whatever answered them at nine at night is where they went.

A page answers at nine at night. That is most of what it does.

How local customers actually find a business now:
https://famtasticdesigns.com/blog/how-local-customers-find-your-business-online/

drops.label: Drop 3 — Tue 8:40 AM ET: "I'm not technical."
drops.theme: Objection 3 — you will not touch it, and neither does anyone else who has one
drops.headline: You are not technical. You will not need to be.

copy.facebook_instagram:
"I'm not technical."

You will not need to be. Nobody who has a website built for them touches the machinery — not the people you assume are more comfortable with this than you are.

The division of labour is short enough to say in one breath.

You answer questions about your own business. What you do, who you serve, what a good customer looks like. Those are the ones only you can answer.

We build the page, host it, and keep it running.

You never open a file.

drops.label: Drop 4 — Wed 6:30 PM ET: "I tried before and got burned."
drops.theme: Objection 4 — name the pattern, then reverse it
drops.headline: You paid up front. You never saw proof. Then the calls stopped.

copy.facebook_instagram:
"I tried before and I got burned."

Let us name the pattern out loud, because it is nearly always the same one.

You paid up front. You never saw proof. Then the calls stopped.

That is not a reason to be suspicious of websites. It is a reason to be suspicious of that order.

FAMtastic runs it the other way around:

01 — You describe your business.
02 — Three real designs of it get built, and a person reviews them before you see them.
03 — You choose one. Then you pay.

If you do not like any of the three, you have not paid for anything.

The whole proof-first flow, written out:
https://famtasticdesigns.com/blog/proof-first-website-see-before-you-pay/

Web Basics is a one-time $199 — first year $199, then $9.99 a month, plus the domain.

drops.label: Drop 5 — Thu 12:00 PM ET: "It's too expensive."
drops.theme: Objection 5 — the whole number, including what renews
drops.headline: $199 for the first year. About 55 cents a day. Then $9.99 a month, plus the domain.

copy.facebook_instagram:
"A website is too expensive."

Here is the whole number, with nothing held back for later.

First year — $199. That is about 55 cents a day.
Every month after that — $9.99.
The domain — billed separately.
Business email — a separate product.
Maintenance — a separate product.

That is all of it. No retainer, no minimum term, no line you find out about in month four.

What the $199 covers: one focused page, one year of managed hosting, and a domain that belongs to you — a new one, or the one you already own connected up.

The arithmetic, written out:
https://famtasticdesigns.com/blog/professional-website-55-cents-a-day/

drops.label: Drop 6 — Sun 10:20 AM ET: "I'm too close to retiring."
drops.theme: Objection 6 — a buyer buys what transfers
drops.headline: Whoever buys this business buys what transfers. A domain transfers.

copy.facebook_instagram:
"I'm too close to retiring."

Then it matters more, not less.

Whoever buys this business buys what transfers. A domain transfers. A page transfers. Thirty years of people knowing your name does not — that walks out the door with you on the last day, and the buyer starts over on the part you were best at.

An address the business owns is one of the few things you can actually hand somebody.
